newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Astrologer to quit if Venezuelan leader stays.
newsitem.headline: Astrologer to quit if Venezuelan leader stays.

text.p: An astrologer detained for predicting that Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera will be forced from office next year pledged on Saturday to quit his trade if his forecast failed to come true.
"If Caldera is still in power by June 8 and nothing has happened to him I'll quit astrology," Jose Bernardo Gomez told El Nacional daily newspaper.

"Caldera has Pluto ascending ... Pluto is the planet of death," said the astrologer, whose detention on Wednesday left political commentators wondering why the government was apparently so nervous about the president's health.
Gomez, president of Venezuela's astrologers' association, was released on Thursday. He told a new conference on Oct. 12 that "Caldera will not pass 1997."
Caldera, now serving his second presidential term, will be 81 in January. His five-year mandate ends in February 1999.
Interior Minister Jose Guillermo Andueza said secret police had detained and questioned the astrologer to investigate the "political implications" of his predictions.

Gomez, who predicted Caldera's surprise election triumph in 1993 and is said to be one of the best in his field, told El Nacional that the "most critical period for President Caldera and for Venezuela will be between Feb. 5 and April 27, 1997."
